High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant/accused under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with Crime No. 18/2024, registered at Police Station M.P Nagar, Bhopal, District Bhopal (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 341, 506 and 195A of the IPC.

2. As per prosecution story, the allegation against the present applicant is that on 08.01.2024 when the complainant came to Court at Bhopal to get information about her case, then outside the Court room in the corridors of the Court the applicant stopped her and threatened her to give false evidence to get the accused acquitted in the case arsing out of crime no.449 of 2023, else he would kill her.
Therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and falsely implicated in the present case.
At the time of commission of offence he was with one Raja Lal at Hotel Surya.
The complainant made a concocted story against the applicant.

Earlier also the Mukesh Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137240385/
1 prosecutrix has lodged a false case against the applicant for offence under Section 376 of IPC in which he has been enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Initially the case was registered under Section 341 and 506 of IPC.
Both are bailable offence but later on, Section 195A of IPC was added.

He further submitted that police cannot register the case under Section 195A of IPC and in support of his submission, he has placed reliance in the case of Shivam @ Shyamsundar Sharma Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh passed in Cr.R.No.618/2023 dated 12.05.2023 and in the case of Smt. Lalita Yadav and others Vs.
State of Madhya Pradesh passed in M.Cr.C.No.76/2014 on 11.09.2014.

entities.text: Shivam @ Shyamsundar Sharma Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh

State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no need of custodial interrogation from the present applicant.
He is ready to co-operate the investigation.
In these circumstances, applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4 . Learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector have opposed the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
It is submitted that in this case applicant has threatened the prosecutrix and there is also one eye witness Ranjeet Singh.
In this matter, the offence is registered under Sections 341, 506 and 195A of IPC and Police can register the offence under Section 195A alongwith the other sections.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix's statements were not recorded in the offence registered under Section 376 of IPC, therefore, he was threatening her.

In support of his arguments, learned counsel for the objector has placed reliance in the case of Abdul Razzak Vs.
State of Madhya Pradesh passed in M.Cr.C.No.26575/2023 on 18.12.2023.
5.

entities.text:
Abdul Razzak Vs.
State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.
6. Consequently, this anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE anu Mukesh Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137240385/
